title: A width CV bound of 0.30 permitted negative squared-width contrasts in six North Wales harebell domes in 2021
abstract: We tested whether unknown width dispersion can change two count-weighted squared-width interaction indices in a 2021 North Wales ozone and warming experiment. We used 24 harebell summary cells from six domes and four monthly visits. Under a conditional moment model, the zero-dispersion contrasts were 36.75 and 32.94 mm squared. Sharp bounds first permit zero at width coefficient of variation caps of 0.278 and 0.266. A cap of 0.30 permits both contrasts to be negative with the same shared-control settings and all released means fixed. Equal dispersion across cells preserves the signs. This is a sensitivity result, not an estimate of actual variation or flower area. One dome per treatment, unknown aggregation, selected flowers and one site-year prevent causal or regional claims. External source records are not bundled. Code, aggregate bounds, source hashes, a figure and independent moment checks support reproduction.

display.caption: Sharp conditional bounds for squared-width contrasts. Unknown cell CV values lie between zero and the horizontal-axis cap. The orange line marks the first cap that permits zero. No sampling uncertainty is shown.

citations.reason: Same source and six-dome four-month scope; new second-moment bounds, not independent biological validation. No code reused.
Unknown count aggregation limits the meaning of fixed count weights.
